issues.title: Large radix aggregate slows 17-35% when more base-table blocks are resident
issues.hypothesis: Reproduced in ONE process (not a bench artifact): q18 is 505-550ms; after q09 (or after just `SELECT sum(l_extendedprice+l_discount+l_partkey+l_suppkey) FROM lineitem; SELECT sum(ps_supplycost) FROM partsupp; SELECT max(p_name) FROM part`) it becomes 630-720ms and stays slow on every later run. The isolated 15M-group agg `SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity)>312)` goes 458/465ms -> 554-654ms. duckdb_memory() BASE_TABLE goes 369MB -> 881-1067MB. A 15M-row probe HJ (orders x lineitem, l_quantity>49) is unaffected (~110ms). SET allocator_flush_threshold / allocator_bulk_deallocation_flush_threshold = 64GB does NOT fix it. memory_limit is 12.2GB, so this is not eviction pressure. TemporaryMemoryManager::UpdateState (temporary_memory_manager.cpp:121-160) does not read used base-table memory, so the reservation is probably not the cause (to verify). This likely explains why E0009/E0013 (q13 large perfect HA) were retired for q18 +8-10%. In the official bench every template runs with lots of columns resident, so q18's 545ms and q13's 2.09s agg likely include this penalty.
issues.plan:
1) Localize: in one dbe-tool sql call run the agg reproducer 3x, load the extra columns, run 3x again, with EXPLAIN ANALYZE / json profiling before and after. Compare TABLE_SCAN CPU vs HASH_GROUP_BY CPU, and if possible sink vs finalize. Use the InternalException-gated-on-setting trick to dump GetThreadLimit() (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:163), the reservation, the radix bits and whether the agg went external/abandoned (lines 484-519) in both states.
2) Hypotheses, in order:
(a) Sink thread limit or radix bits differ (reservation or ComputeReservation depends on state) -> fix the computation.
(b) BlockAllocator pool (block_allocator.cpp): base-table loads take the 'touched' blocks the agg freed, so the agg's TupleDataCollection blocks land in other pool regions with worse TLB/THP backing. Try madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE) on the pool mmap in AllocateVirtualMemory (:33, Linux only) and check that OnDeallocation's MADV_DONTNEED isn't splitting huge pages on frequently reused blocks.
(c) Eviction-queue / pin-unpin cost grows with the number of resident blocks (buffer_pool.cpp AddToEvictionQueue/PurgeQueue).
3) Land only a mechanism that removes the gap in the reproducer and that does not change behavior under memory pressure.
issues.expected_gain: q18 -10..-15% (its agg dominates). Possibly q13 (2.09s agg CPU) and q16 a few %. Visible geomean -1..-2% if found.
issues.generality: Any large hash aggregation on a warm database with many cached columns, which is the normal hot-run state. If the fix is an allocator/THP change, it affects all buffer-managed memory; queries with small memory footprints should be neutral.
issues.risk: Medium-high on discovery: the cause may be OS-level and unfixable, and the round may yield nothing. Implementation risk is low once localized. A THP madvise could raise RSS.

issues.title: Large perfect HA v3 after the resident-memory agg fix
issues.hypothesis: E0009/E0013 gave q13 -17..-23% in 10/10 runs but were retired for q18 +8.7%. The in-process reproducer shows q18's agg slows whenever memory state changes (more resident blocks), so that regression was the same phenomenon as the resident-memory issue, not a cost of the perfect HA. Once that issue lands, re-landing E0013 should clear q13's 14% threshold without the q18 hit.
issues.plan: Re-apply E0013 as described in the ledger: plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate up to 22 bits with the density, memory and no-DELIM guards; is_large-only code paths in physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp (lazy init, striped combine, parallel source, buffer-allocator tables). Before benchmarking, check in-process that q18 after q13 is unchanged.
issues.generality: GROUP BY on dense integer keys up to 4M range with many input rows per group (FK group-bys).
issues.risk: Medium: q18 regressed twice before. Dispatch only after the resident-memory issue lands or is understood.

issues.title: Faster substring search: rare-pair candidate test + exact multi-literal LIKE in prefilter
issues.hypothesis: Orders scan, sum(o_custkey): with NOT LIKE '%special%packages%' 148-166ms; with '%packages%' alone ~155-160ms; with '%zzzqx%' ~110ms; length() only ~95ms. So the cost of finding 'packages' (2.25M/15M rows hit) is ~50ms of wall over decode. FindSubstring (column_segment.cpp:665) matches on the first/last char 'p'/'s', which are common, then calls memcmp per candidate.
issues.plan: In FindSubstring, use an 8-byte load+mask compare for needle_len<=9 instead of memcmp, and choose the candidate-pair chars from the needle's rarer bytes. Optionally, for patterns of only '%' wildcards, match all literals in order inside the run so hits are exact and SelectExpression is skipped.
issues.expected_gain: q13 -5..-9% (below its 14% noise threshold alone); small gains on any LIKE scan.
issues.generality: All LIKE/contains scan filters on long strings.
issues.risk: Low; correctness depends on exact boundary handling.

- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run. Treat them as strong priors.

## KEY FINDING r14: resident base-table memory slows the big radix agg (in-process)
- q18: 505-550ms -> 630-720ms after q09 OR after just loading extra columns (lineitem l_extendedprice/l_discount/l_partkey/l_suppkey, partsupp, part). It stays slow on every later run.
- Isolated agg `SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity)>312)`: 460 -> 540-650ms. A 15M-probe HJ is unaffected.
- BASE_TABLE memory 369 -> 881-1067MB; memory_limit 12.2GB; threads 8.
- allocator_flush_threshold / bulk_deallocation thresholds = 64GB do NOT fix it.
- This explains the E0009/E0013 "q18 artifact": it is real engine/OS state, not the perfect HA.
- Candidate causes: sink reservation/thread limit, BlockAllocator touched/untouched block reuse + THP/TLB, eviction-queue cost.
- read_text on /sys and /proc fails (size-0 files).

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Any template slower beyond noise gets the issue retired.
- Bundle a near-miss with a general second mechanism hitting the SAME template (worked in E0021, E0027, E0029).

## Measured r14
- q09 plan: HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 1.37s CPU (build 3.27M lineitem side, probe 2.94M orders); lineitem scan 3.57s CPU (60M rows, BF(l_partkey) + min/max); HJ partkey/suppkey 0.61s; part contains scan 0.33s.
- Plain full scan of l_partkey over 60M = 24ms hot wall. Selecting 2 columns at 5% sel adds ~15ms; 3 more adds ~17ms.
- q13 orders scan: FSST decode ~95ms wall; 'packages' search adds ~50ms ('p'/'s' first/last are common chars); prefilter uses the longest literal, then SelectExpression on hits.

## Key finding r13: q07
- HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 0.48s CPU builds 1.46M rows (wide payload) and probes 100k. Build cost is superlinear (330ns/row). Flipping does not help.
- Scan filters already use AdaptiveFilter (row_group.cpp:759). Do not propose filter reordering.

## Codebase facts
- Perfect HJ BF: CanUseBloomFilter + PushPerfectHashJoinBloomFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp); PerfectHashJoinExecutor::FillExactBloomFilter. The perfect HT range can come from static stats, while the BF range comes from dynamic min/max.
- BitPacking: bitpacking.cpp (Select ~886, per-value when sel*4<=count). DELTA_FOR still decodes everything.
- TEMP tables are never compressed.
- Substring prefilter: column_segment.cpp:662-860 (FindSubstring SSE2, GetSubstringPrefilter, TrySubstringPrefilter).
- Radix agg memory: radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp GetThreadLimit :163, external/abandon :484-519. TemporaryMemoryManager::UpdateState :121.
- BlockAllocator: block_allocator.cpp (mmap pool :33, prefault OnFirstAllocation :50, MADV_DONTNEED :77, touched/untouched queues). BufferPool FlushAll is called when extra_memory > 512MB.
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp. Join filters: join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp. Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: fsst.cpp. BF: bloom_filter.cpp; exact BF fill in join_hashtable.cpp ~731-769; HT insert InsertHashesLoop :591.

## How to measure
- Micro A/B: CREATE TEMP VIEW a/b; `from a; from b;` alternated, all in one dbe-tool sql call (each call is a new process; the first query is cold). Do NOT wrap in count(*) when the plan matters.
- Full operator timings: SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='<slot>/.dbe/scratch_x.json'. /tmp is not readable.
- dbe-tool profile qNN.m0 works; pipe through grep to trim.
- Bash: only dbe-tool. Pipes work for grep/tail, but `grep -v "^$"` needs approval.
- Bench noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20%, q04 ~20%, q07 ~13%.

## Profile snapshot (r14): q18 545, q13 525, q09 414, q05 207, q16 207, q03 180, q07 178, q08 158, q04 145, q17 119, q14 116, q22 105, q19 95, q02 57. Geomean 176.8.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe, CM fold decompress/compress (q13).
- Allocator flush thresholds as the fix for the resident-memory slowdown (tested r14, no effect).

## Next candidates (round 15-16)
1. If r14 finds and fixes the cause: dispatch Large perfect HA v3 (q13 -20%).
2. If r14 fails: either bundle the substring search speedup with another q13 mechanism, or try DELTA_FOR select / BitPacking threshold tuning.
3. Large HJ builds (q09 1.37s, q07 0.48s, q03 0.34s): partitioned build is a big change; HJ prefetch was dead.
